source_spans.locator: Cognitive Psychology 4(1), published pp.55-58, Abstract, Introduction, Scope, and Method: three players (master, Class A, beginner) perform a visible reconstruction task and a reconstruction-after-5-second-view task on actual and randomized positions; successive glances and long inter-piece pauses are used as operational boundaries for inferred grouped representations

Cognitive Psychology 4(1), published pp.59-62, Accuracy of Reconstruction/Figs.1-2: first-trial correct placements after five-second viewing increase strongly with playing strength for actual positions, while randomized positions show no relation between recall accuracy and playing strength

Cognitive Psychology 4(1), published pp.63-70, perception-task timing and relation analyses: more skilled players require less viewing time per glance; average pieces per glance does not vary systematically with playing strength; within-glance piece pairs show nonchance relational structure

Cognitive Psychology 4(1), published pp.70-75, comparison of visible-reconstruction and brief-recall protocols: short inter-piece pauses in recall have relation profiles similar to within-glance placements, while long pauses resemble between-glance/chance structure, supporting the operational grouping interpretation

Cognitive Psychology 4(1), published pp.75-78, group-size and retained-group analysis: in the brief-recall task group size is larger for stronger players, and the number of retained groups also increases with playing strength rather than remaining invariant; this challenges a simple fixed list of unrelated immediate-storage slots

Cognitive Psychology 4(1), published pp.78-80, detailed master protocols: most identified multi-piece groups belong to a small set of highly familiar stereotyped configuration classes; some groups also reflect more abstract converging-attack relations

Cognitive Psychology 4(1), published pp.80-81, Conclusion: stronger-player advantage on actual but not randomized positions is interpreted as rapid encoding of familiar subconfigurations into larger grouped representations; within-group relations include mutual defense, proximity, short-distance attack, common color/type, with possible higher-order organization

conditions: actual game-derived positions compared with positions produced by randomly relocating the same kinds and approximate numbers of pieces
middle-game and end-game configurations are both tested, with structure differing across position types
population: three players: one master, one Class A player, and one beginner
task: reconstruct a displayed board while it remains visible
reconstruct a board from memory after five seconds of viewing
temporal_scope: first and subsequent reconstruction attempts following five-second exposures, with primary accuracy analysis focused on the first attempt

nodes.description: relative playing level of the master, Class A participant, and beginner
whether a tested configuration comes from an actual game or from random relocation of pieces
middle-game versus end-game configuration, which differs in amount and organization of available relational structure
reconstruct the displayed configuration while viewing is allowed, using successive glances to segment placements
reconstruct the configuration after five seconds of viewing, using placement timing to segment the recall protocol
number of pieces placed on the correct squares on the first reconstruction attempt after a five-second view
time spent viewing the source configuration during each glance in the visible reconstruction task
number of successively placed pieces associated with one glance in the visible reconstruction task
time between placement of successive pieces during reconstruction
set of successively placed pieces operationally inferred to belong together when they fall within one glance or between short placement intervals
number of pieces contained in an operationally inferred group
number of operationally inferred groups placed during the initial recall phase before later reconstructive problem solving
nonchance pattern of relations among pieces placed within an inferred group, including defense, proximity, short-distance attack, common color, and common type
source-authored interpretation that stronger players possess a stored repertoire capable of rapidly recognizing familiar multi-piece subconfigurations

relations.description: first-attempt reconstruction after five seconds improves markedly with playing strength for actual game-derived positions, while randomized positions show no corresponding strength advantage
successive glances in the visible task provide one operational segmentation of grouped placements and their processing time
more skilled participants take less viewing time per glance in the visible reconstruction task
the number of pieces associated with each glance does not vary systematically with playing strength, so the visible-task advantage is not a simple larger-group effect on this measure
short versus long placement intervals provide a second operational segmentation whose relation profiles correspond to within- versus between-glance placements
in the brief-recall protocol, early inferred groups are generally larger for stronger players, with smaller groups in less structured end-game positions
the number of inferred groups retained during initial recall also increases with playing strength, contrary to the source's initial prediction of an invariant small count
pieces grouped by the timing/glance criteria show stronger relational organization within groups than across group boundaries or chance baselines

the authors interpret the stronger-player advantage on actual positions as rapid recognition and encoding of familiar multi-piece subconfigurations into larger grouped representations rather than as a generally superior ability to retain arbitrary configurations

because stronger players recall both larger and more numerous groups, the data do not support a simple model in which all players retain an invariant fixed list of unrelated groups; the source leaves higher-order organization and reconstruction from stored configuration knowledge as alternative explanations
